Hmm, what if the goal is to move the gray so that the gray's cells align with the positions mirrored from the black's dots? That is, the gray should cover the mirror positions of the black's dots? The black's dot mirror positions: (19,28),(19,25),(19,22),(22,22),(25,22),(28,22),(28,19),(28,16). Does the gray (top 15-23) cover (19,22)? Row 19 is within the top bar (18-20), columns 15-23 → yes, (19,22) is covered. (19,25)? No. So it's not fully covered.
This is getting too speculative. Let me try MOUSE: click on the black piece, or click on the yellow, and see if something happens (selection, movement, etc.). Also try clicking on the divider.
No, wait. Let me reconsider. What if the gray piece is a "shadow" and the actual player piece is the black, and the black moves... The black didn't move with any arrow key. What if the black moves with MOUSE clicks? Or what if the black moves when the gray's mirror overlaps it (like a "push")?

The yellow is at top 9-17, bottom 3-11. One more LEFT would make the gray's top 9-17, bottom 3-11 = exactly the yellow's column. Then maybe the gray falls down (DOWN works after alignment?) or the level is cleared.
Let me try: LEFT once (gray's top 9-17), then DOWN and see if anything happens.
